title: Billing cycle
text: Orbit Analytics bills on a monthly cycle by default. Your invoice is generated on the same calendar day you first subscribed, and charges are collected automatically from the card on file.

title: Annual billing discount
text: Switching from monthly to annual billing applies a 20 percent discount to your plan. The change takes effect immediately and any unused portion of the current month is credited to your account.

title: Downloading invoices
text: Invoices are available under Settings, Billing, Invoices. Each invoice can be downloaded as a PDF and includes your company address and tax identifier if one has been saved.

title: VAT and GST identifiers
text: Adding a VAT or GST identifier to your billing profile removes tax from future invoices in supported regions. Previously issued invoices cannot be amended retroactively.

title: Refund policy
text: Refunds are issued for the current billing period only and must be requested within fourteen days of the charge. Annual plans cancelled mid term are refunded on a pro rata basis.

title: Cancelling a subscription
text: You can cancel a subscription at any time from Settings, Billing. Your workspace stays on the paid plan until the end of the period already paid for, then reverts to the free tier.

title: Downgrading a plan
text: Downgrading to the free plan keeps all historical data but limits querying to the most recent ninety days. No events are deleted by a downgrade.

title: Free trial
text: New workspaces start with a fourteen day trial of the Growth plan. No card is required to begin the trial and the workspace is not charged when it ends.

title: Seat pricing
text: Seats are billed per active member per month. Members who have not signed in for sixty days are marked inactive automatically and are not charged.

title: Failed payments
text: If a card payment fails we retry three times over seven days. The workspace keeps full access during the retry window and an email is sent to every workspace administrator.

title: Creating API keys
text: Create an API key under Settings, Developers, API Keys. Keys are shown once at creation time and cannot be retrieved afterwards, so store the value in your own secret manager.

title: Rotating API keys
text: Rotating a key issues a new secret and keeps the old one valid for twenty four hours, which lets you deploy the replacement without downtime.

title: Ingest rate limits
text: The ingest endpoint accepts sixty requests per second per API key. Requests beyond that limit receive HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header indicating how long to wait.

title: Batching events
text: To stay under the ingest limit, batch up to five hundred events into a single request. Batched events are counted individually against your monthly event quota but as one request against the rate limit.

title: HTTP error codes
text: A 401 response means the API key is missing or revoked, 403 means the key lacks the required scope, and 422 means the event payload failed schema validation.

title: Browser SDK install
text: Install the browser SDK with npm install orbit-analytics, then call orbit.init with your public project token. The SDK queues events while offline and flushes them on reconnect.

title: Mobile SDKs
text: The iOS and Android SDKs are distributed through Swift Package Manager and Maven Central. Both buffer events locally and retry delivery with exponential backoff.

title: Webhooks
text: Webhooks deliver a signed POST to your endpoint when an alert fires or an export finishes. Verify the signature header before trusting the payload.

title: Webhook retries
text: A webhook that does not return a 2xx status within five seconds is retried with exponential backoff for up to six hours, after which the delivery is dropped and logged.

title: Custom events
text: Custom events are created simply by sending them. An event name is limited to sixty four characters and each event may carry up to one hundred properties.

title: Single sign on
text: Single sign on is available on the Enterprise plan and supports any SAML 2.0 identity provider, including Okta, Entra ID and Google Workspace.

title: SCIM provisioning
text: SCIM provisioning keeps workspace membership in sync with your directory. Removing a user in the identity provider revokes their Orbit session within five minutes.

title: Two factor authentication
text: Two factor authentication can be enforced for every member from Settings, Security. Members without 2FA are prompted to enrol at their next sign in and cannot skip it.

title: Password reset
text: Use the forgot password link on the sign in screen to receive a reset email. The link expires after one hour and can only be used once.

title: Roles and permissions
text: Orbit has four roles: Owner, Admin, Analyst and Viewer. Only Owners can change billing, and only Owners and Admins can create or revoke API keys.

title: IP allowlist
text: An IP allowlist can be applied to the dashboard, the API, or both. Requests from outside the listed ranges are refused before authentication is attempted.

title: Audit log
text: The audit log records sign ins, permission changes, key creation and data exports, and retains twelve months of history on the Enterprise plan.

title: Session timeout
text: Dashboard sessions expire after thirty days of inactivity by default. Enterprise workspaces can shorten this to as little as one hour.

title: Data retention
text: Raw event data is retained for twelve months on Growth and twenty four months on Enterprise. Aggregated metrics are kept indefinitely and are unaffected by raw data expiry.

title: Personal data deletion
text: A deletion request for an individual removes their events and profile within thirty days across primary storage and backups. A confirmation report is available once processing completes.

title: Data residency
text: Workspaces can be provisioned in the European Union or United States region. The region is fixed at creation time and cannot be changed without a full migration.

title: Subprocessors
text: A current list of subprocessors is published on the trust page, and customers on annual contracts are notified thirty days before any new subprocessor is added.

title: CSV export
text: Any table or chart can be exported to CSV from the menu in its top right corner. Exports above one hundred thousand rows are prepared asynchronously and emailed as a download link.

title: Warehouse connectors
text: The Snowflake and BigQuery connectors sync raw events on an hourly schedule. The first sync backfills the full retention window and can take several hours.

title: CSV import
text: Historical data can be imported from CSV provided each row carries an event name and a timestamp in ISO 8601 format. Imported events count towards your monthly quota.

title: Funnels
text: A funnel measures how many users complete an ordered sequence of steps within a conversion window. Steps can be reordered without recomputing the underlying data.

title: Cohort analysis
text: Cohort analysis groups users by the week they first appeared and tracks their return behaviour over subsequent weeks, which is the fastest way to see whether retention is improving.

title: Segments
text: Segments are saved filters over user or event properties. A segment can be applied to any report, and updating the segment definition updates every report that uses it.

title: Dashboards
text: Dashboards hold up to fifty charts and refresh on an interval you choose. A dashboard can be shared with a public read only link that hides the underlying raw data.

title: Alerts
text: Alerts watch a metric and notify you through email, Slack or a webhook when a threshold is crossed. Alerts are evaluated every fifteen minutes.

title: Session replay
text: Session replay records user interaction in the browser and masks all input fields by default. Replays are retained for thirty days regardless of plan.

title: Query sampling
text: Reports over very large workspaces may be sampled to keep queries fast. The sampling rate is always displayed on the chart and can be disabled for exact counts at the cost of slower queries.

title: Report timezone
text: Reports are rendered in the workspace timezone, not the viewer local time. Changing the workspace timezone re-buckets historical data on the next query.

title: Reporting currency
text: Revenue metrics are displayed in the workspace reporting currency. Values sent in other currencies are converted using the exchange rate on the day the event was received.

title: Identity resolution
text: Anonymous activity is merged into a user profile as soon as you call identify with a stable user identifier. Events recorded before the call are retroactively attributed to that user.

title: Slack integration
text: The Slack integration posts alert notifications to a channel you choose. Installing it requires a Slack workspace administrator to approve the requested scopes.

title: Status page
text: Live service status and incident history are published on the status page, and subscribing there sends email updates when an incident is opened or resolved.

title: Support response targets
text: Growth plans receive a first response within one business day. Enterprise plans include a four hour response target for critical issues and a named technical contact.

title: Sandbox project
text: Every workspace includes a free sandbox project for testing. Events sent to the sandbox never appear in production reports and do not count towards your quota.

title: API versioning
text: API versions are pinned per key and remain supported for at least eighteen months after a successor is released. Deprecation notices are sent by email and shown in the dashboard.

title: Quota overage
text: Exceeding your monthly event quota does not stop ingestion. Overage is billed at the published per event rate on your next invoice, and a warning is emailed at eighty percent of quota.

title: Uptime commitment
text: The Enterprise agreement includes a 99.9 percent monthly uptime commitment with service credits applied automatically to the following invoice when it is missed.

title: Transferring ownership
text: Ownership of a workspace can be transferred to another member from Settings, General. The outgoing owner keeps Admin access unless removed separately.

title: Deleting a workspace
text: Deleting a workspace is irreversible and removes all projects, events and dashboards after a seven day grace period during which it can still be restored by support.

title: Mobile companion app
text: The mobile companion app shows dashboards and alerts but cannot create or edit reports. It is available for iOS and Android and uses the same sign in as the web dashboard.

title: Migrating from another tool
text: Migration from another analytics tool is supported through the import API and a mapping file that translates legacy event names to your Orbit taxonomy.
